text: I'm going to say it, I'm going to say it, and you're not going to like what I have to say. You're not going to like it, man. You're not going to like it. Where are the real men at? I'm sick of it. They don't make men like they used to. I'm going to say it loud and proud, because tell me why men these days, they don't want to do an oil change. They don't know how to change a tire. They don't know how to do anything. If Google doesn't know, babe, they don't know. Okay, let's break this down. She says men today aren't real men because they can't change a tire or do an oil change. First of all, let's be honest here. Having some know-how with tools and fixes never hurts. But let's also not act like turning a wrench is the ultimate definition of masculinity. Our dad's generation grew up in a different world. No YouTube tutorials, no Google, no apps to book a handyman in five minutes. Of course, they learned to fix everything themselves. Today, men can specialize. Some guys run companies, trade stocks, build tech, work as lawyers. And yeah, maybe they pay someone else to do their oil change. That doesn't make them less of a man. And here's the irony. Most women today don't know how to cook a full meal from scratch, sew clothes, or run a household the way their grandmothers did. Times change, skills evolve. But notice, when it comes to men, suddenly we're supposed to still live like it's 1950. That being said, guys, I'll still say this. Don't be useless. Learn how to handle everyday tasks, be reliable, and take care of things. Not because it makes you a real man, but because it makes you a functional adult. So yes, old school skills can be valuable. But masculinity is more than manual labor. It's competence, confidence, and the ability to take responsibility, whether that's fixing something or building a future.
